newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Buba rate remarks boost Belgian linear bonds.
newsitem.headline: Buba rate remarks boost Belgian linear bonds.

text.p: Remarks by Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp indicating there might be room for a rate cut put a rocket under Belgian bonds on Thursday, powering the March futures to a new contract high at one stage.

The comment was all the latent bull sentiment underpinning the market needed to break loose despite recent emerging fears that what had been going up so strongly for so long had at some stage to come thumping back down again.
Traders said the market, which had started the day in a lethargic manner, exploded into life as Krupp's comments also boosted Bunds. They were unsure what would happen next.
"Most of the business between market-makers was in these two OLOs," one trader said.

The yield of the new benchmark 2007 OLO ended the day at 5.78 percent against Thursday's closing 5.84 percent, but the spread over Bunds, which fluctuated during the day, ended at an unchanged seven basis points.
The March futures contract finished 43 basis higher at 121.79, having at one stage hit a new contract high of 121.95.
"We went up on Krupp's comments together with Bunds. This morning we saw the 10-year spread stabilising, but it has now come in again," one trader said.
Traders said the focus of business was, as in recent days, the very long maturities -- particularly the 10- to 20-year linear bonds.
"Some people have sold Belgian OLOs against Bunds," one added.
Traders noted most interest in OLOs 12 and 23 -- maturing in December 2012 and March 2015.
